title: Which Partial-Experiment Menus Identify Full-Treatment Response Laws in Acyclic Treatment Systems
banked_reason: The proof is sound and complete, but the cold tier gate capped it at subfield (6.5) below the field floor (7.4), with no credible in-scope repair.
gap_reasons: The result concerns full-arm marginal laws, with no characterization of their cross-world coupling or inference from sampled experiments.

The only worked menu illustrates coefficient cancellation without a concrete source-law or decision example, limiting the package's demonstrated econometric significance and its projected leading-journal score.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the ambient-class iff menu criterion, strictly positive finite countermodels, finite response-table reduction, and the exact simultaneous translated-simplex identified set with source-preserving finite attainment. Math and decision referees passed, but the cold tier review found the package below the field floor because it identifies marginal laws only and adds neither sampled-data inference nor a substantive application. Clearing the floor would require a new research axis such as cross-world coupling, inference theory, or data-dependent geometry for nonqualifying menus rather than an in-scope repair.
tldr: Complete partial experiments in a finite acyclic treatment system reveal a consistency-covered part of each full-treatment categorical outcome law. With a saturated final outcome and one unrestricted common exogenous state, the nonzero-intersection-coefficient condition exactly characterizes menus that identify these covered sublaws for every compatible source collection. For such menus, the identified set over the standard possibly infinite-exogenous NPSEM class is a simultaneous product of translated categorical simplices. Every product point has one finite source-preserving SCM witness.
gap: Existing logical bounds and canonical response-type programs do not, in the inspected results, classify when an arbitrary complete partial-experiment menu reveals its consistency-covered sublaws or give a simultaneous closed-form categorical projection.
fill: Prove the universal coefficient criterion, its explicit positive countermodels, and the joint translated-simplex theorem, including a source-preserving finite witness for all arm marginals at once.
